body:
I'm not sure if this solution is a better solution than the one that Godot Physics has chosen where the first call to set transform after making a body kinematic teleports the object. Subsequent calls only set the 'desired transform'.

The main problem that I see with this PR is what you already mention: physics queries. Let's say I want to make a game about shooting arrows and I want those arrows to stick to the enemy. I do a ray cast to find the collision between the arrow and the enemy. This will [return](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/physics/ray-casting.html) a world space position and the enemy collider. I get the transform of the collider, calculate the hit position relative to that collider and then parent the arrow to the collider. If the 'get transform' function returns the 'desired transform' instead of the 'current transform' and the 'cast ray' function returns collisions with the object still being at 'current transform', my calculation is off and the arrow sticks in the wrong spot. Since there's no API to get the 'current transform' after this change, I don't think it is possible to make my arrow work.

So my vote would be for replicating the 'first_time_kinematic' behavior of Godot Physics. If we're allowed to make a breaking change to the Godot API then I would vote for making a `move_body_kinematic` function that sets the desired transform. The `set_transform` call can then just teleport the body.

Edit: And to ease the transition you could add the `move_body_kinematic` call and have a project setting that determines if we want the old or new behavior for `set_transform`.
Closing, since something like #113784 is likely the better approach here.
